correctness.rationale: The checker constructs all 2^15 edge subsets twice, as (i) degree tests and (ii) ten forbidden full stars. Both select exactly 10,895 faces including the empty face. Repeated increasing-index toggles yield 5,447 disjoint augmented pairs and one unmatched seven-edge face. After removing only the empty/singleton pair, the ordinary face poset has 5,446 pairs and exactly one critical 0-cell and one 6-cell. Each of its 64,005 Hasse incidences is reoriented according to this matching; Kahn's algorithm visits all 10,894 nonempty faces, proving acyclicity. Forman discrete Morse theory then gives a CW complex with exactly these two cells; the sole six-cell attaches to a point, hence the homotopy type S6. All quantifiers are finite and exhaustively checked; no inferred infinite-family theorem.

originality.rationale: Vega 2019 gives general definitions and special graph families, not the pentagonal-prism case; Singh 2020 classifies complete/complete bipartite higher matchings; Agarwal–Basak 2026 studies independence and perfect-matching complexes of the same prism family but not M2. Targeted indexed searches and prior scientific-claim comparisons found no statement implying the new six-sphere classification; overlapping source titles alone were not treated as proof. Residual bibliographic and history-access risks remain explicit.
residual_risks: Database/search retrieval is incomplete and cannot establish uniqueness; an unindexed equivalence or unpublished complete circular-ladder two-matching theorem could exist.
This is an exact single-graph result; no general formula for all circular ladders is proved.
The proof gives a nonequivariant homotopy equivalence; it does not compute the induced dihedral action on the sphere orientation.

value.rationale: The pentagonal prism is the smallest odd circular ladder after the triangular prism, and a canonical vertex-transitive cubic polyhedral graph. Its ordinary one-matching complex has homology in two dimensions, whereas relaxing the bound to two gives an unexpected single six-sphere despite nonpure faces reaching dimension nine. The exact 10,894-face Morse reduction is a meaningful complete benchmark for degree-bounded complexes on cyclic cubic graphs, without claiming an entire family theorem.
